questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.prompt: At a streaming service, 0.35 of subscribers enable download notifications, and 0.12 enable both download notifications and dark mode. What is the probability that a randomly selected subscriber enables download notifications but does not enable dark mode?
questions.explanation: Subtract the overlap from the probability of notifications: P(notifications and not dark mode) = 0.35 − 0.12 = 0.23.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: A high school wants to estimate the proportion of all students who are satisfied with the school lunch program. Administrators survey a simple random sample drawn only from students who purchased a school lunch that day. What is the primary concern?

choices.A: Students who brought lunch or did not eat are excluded from the sampling frame, creating undercoverage.
choices.B: The use of a simple random sample guarantees that the estimate is unbiased for all students.
choices.C: The sample is a voluntary-response sample because students purchased lunch.
choices.D: The study is an experiment because lunch choice was observed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students who brought lunch or did not eat are excluded from the sampling frame, creating undercoverage.
questions.explanation: Random selection within a restricted frame represents only lunch purchasers. It does not give all students a chance to be selected.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: For the same difference in two population proportions, a 90% confidence interval is (0.010, 0.070), while a 99% confidence interval is (−0.007, 0.087). Which conclusion is justified?

choices.A: Both intervals provide evidence of a positive difference at their corresponding significance levels.
choices.B: The data provide evidence of a positive difference at the 0.10 level but not at the 0.01 level for a two-sided test.
choices.C: The population difference has a 90% probability of being between 0.01 and 0.07.
choices.D: The wider interval proves that the null hypothesis is true at the 0.01 level.

questions.correctAnswerText: The data provide evidence of a positive difference at the 0.10 level but not at the 0.01 level for a two-sided test.
questions.explanation: The 90% interval excludes the null value 0, whereas the 99% interval includes 0. This corresponds to rejecting at α = 0.10 but not at α = 0.01 for two-sided tests.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: In a random sample of 25 devices, the standard error of the sample mean operating time is 1.2 hours. What is the sample standard deviation of operating times?
questions.explanation: For a sample mean, SE = s/√n. Thus s = 1.2√25 = 1.2(5) = 6.0 hours.

questions.unit: Unit 5: Regression Analysis
questions.prompt: A researcher wants to study the relationship between weekly practice time and performance score for a sample of musicians. What should the researcher do first to examine the form, direction, strength, and possible unusual features of the relationship?

choices.A: Construct separate pie charts for practice time and performance score.
choices.B: Compare the two sample means with a two-sample t-test.
choices.C: Make a scatterplot of performance score versus weekly practice time.
choices.D: Fit a regression line without first displaying the paired data.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make a scatterplot of performance score versus weekly practice time.
questions.explanation: A scatterplot is the appropriate first display for two quantitative variables measured on the same individuals. It reveals form, direction, strength, and unusual observations before a model is fitted.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt:
The following ordered data are displayed in a stem-and-leaf plot, where 3|4 represents 34.

2 | 1 4
3 | 0 3 3 5
4 | 2

Which pair gives the median and range, respectively?

choices.A: Median 32; range 18
choices.B: Median 33; range 21
choices.C: Median 33; range 42
choices.D: Median 34; range 21

questions.correctAnswerText: Median 33; range 21
questions.explanation: The seven values are 21, 24, 30, 33, 33, 35, and 42. The fourth value is 33, and the range is 42 − 21 = 21.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: A confidence interval for a population proportion is reported as (0.441, 0.519). The sample proportion is 0.480, and its estimated standard error is 0.020. What confidence level was used, approximately?
questions.explanation: The margin of error is 0.519 − 0.480 = 0.039, so z* = 0.039/0.020 = 1.95, approximately 1.96. That critical value corresponds to about 95% confidence.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.stimulus: A safety panel contains four alert buttons labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4. On each of two independent trials, one label is selected at random, with all four labels equally likely. Let X be the larger of the two selected labels.
questions.prompt: Two alert labels are selected independently and uniformly from 1, 2, 3, and 4, and X is the larger label. What is P(X = 2)?
questions.explanation: X = 2 occurs when both labels are at most 2 but not both are at most 1. Therefore P(X = 2) = (2/4)² − (1/4)² = 4/16 − 1/16 = 3/16.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.stimulus: A safety panel contains four alert buttons labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4. On each of two independent trials, one label is selected at random, with all four labels equally likely. Let X be the larger of the two selected labels.
questions.prompt: Two alert labels are selected independently and uniformly from 1, 2, 3, and 4, and X is the larger label. What is P(X ≥ 3)?
questions.explanation: The complement of X ≥ 3 is that both selected labels are at most 2. Thus P(X ≥ 3) = 1 − (2/4)² = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.stimulus: A safety panel contains four alert buttons labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4. On each of two independent trials, one label is selected at random, with all four labels equally likely. Let X be the larger of the two selected labels.
questions.prompt: Two alert labels are selected independently and uniformly from 1, 2, 3, and 4, and X is the larger label. Which value is a median of the probability distribution of X?
questions.explanation: P(X ≤ 2) = (2/4)² = 0.25, while P(X ≤ 3) = (3/4)² = 0.5625. The cumulative probability first reaches at least 0.5 at X = 3.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: Each participant uses keyboard layout A for one timed task and layout B for a comparable timed task, with the order randomized. If d = time with A − time with B for each participant, which parameter should be the focus of inference?

choices.A: μ_d, the population mean of the within-participant time differences
choices.B: μ_A − μ_B for two independent populations of participants
choices.C: p_A − p_B, the difference in population completion proportions
choices.D: σ_d, the population standard deviation of the within-participant time differences

questions.correctAnswerText: μ_d, the population mean of the within-participant time differences
questions.explanation: Both measurements come from the same participant, so the observations are paired. Inference should be based on the population mean of the defined within-participant differences.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: The mean commute time for 50 employees is 18.4 minutes. Which statement must be true?

choices.A: Exactly half of the employees commute less than 18.4 minutes.
choices.B: At least one employee has a commute time of exactly 18.4 minutes.
choices.C: Most employees commute between 17.4 and 19.4 minutes.
choices.D: The sum of the 50 commute times is 920 minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The sum of the 50 commute times is 920 minutes.
questions.explanation: Since x̄ = Σx/n, the sum is n x̄ = 50(18.4) = 920 minutes. A mean does not determine the median, any individual value, or a narrow concentration of values.

questions.unit: Unit 5: Regression Analysis
questions.prompt: A least-squares regression line predicts a sound rating y from a machine setting x. Every sound rating is then recalibrated by adding 4 units, so y* = y + 4. Which statement describes the regression of y* on x?

choices.A: The slope and correlation are unchanged, and the intercept increases by 4.
choices.B: The slope increases by 4, and the intercept and correlation are unchanged.
choices.C: The slope and intercept both increase by 4, and the correlation decreases.
choices.D: The slope is unchanged, the intercept increases by 4, and the correlation becomes 4r.

questions.correctAnswerText: The slope and correlation are unchanged, and the intercept increases by 4.
questions.explanation: Adding 4 to every response shifts all points and predictions vertically by 4. It does not change standardized association or the amount y changes per unit of x.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: A university wants to estimate the proportion of students who have experienced food insecurity, a sensitive topic. Which data-collection method is most likely to reduce response bias while preserving the ability to take a probability sample?

choices.A: Ask resident assistants to identify students they believe have experienced food insecurity.
choices.B: Interview students face-to-face and require them to state their names.
choices.C: Select students randomly and allow them to complete a confidential, self-administered questionnaire.
choices.D: Post an open survey link on social media and use everyone who responds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Select students randomly and allow them to complete a confidential, self-administered questionnaire.
questions.explanation: Random selection supports representation, and confidential self-administration reduces the social pressure and interviewer effects that can distort answers to sensitive questions.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.prompt: For randomly selected shipments, P(express) = 0.30 and P(damaged | express) = 0.40. What is P(express and damaged)?
questions.explanation: By the multiplication rule, P(express and damaged) = P(express)P(damaged | express) = 0.30(0.40) = 0.12.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: A news organization tells interviewers to obtain 20 adults from each of four age groups at a downtown shopping district. Within each age group, interviewers approach whichever people seem easiest to contact. Which assessment is most appropriate?

choices.A: The design is a randomized block experiment because age groups are used.
choices.B: The equal quotas make the sample a simple random sample of city adults.
choices.C: The design prevents selection bias because every age group has the same sample size.
choices.D: The age quotas do not remove convenience selection within groups, so the sample can be biased.

questions.correctAnswerText: The age quotas do not remove convenience selection within groups, so the sample can be biased.
questions.explanation: Quotas control the number sampled in each age category, but interviewers still choose convenient individuals. Without random selection within groups, inclusion probabilities are unknown and selection bias can remain.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: A one-sample t-test is performed on temperatures measured in degrees Celsius. Every observation and the null mean are converted to degrees Fahrenheit using F = 1.8C + 32. What happens to the t statistic?

choices.A: It is multiplied by 1.8.
choices.B: It increases by 32.
choices.C: It remains unchanged.
choices.D: It is divided by 1.8.

questions.correctAnswerText: It remains unchanged.
questions.explanation: Both x̄ − μ0 and s are multiplied by 1.8 under the conversion, while n is unchanged. The common factor cancels in t = (x̄ − μ0)/(s/√n).

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: A planning study suggests that a population proportion is about 0.20. What minimum sample size is needed so that a 95% confidence interval for the proportion has margin of error at most 0.06? Use z* = 1.96 and the planning value 0.20.
questions.explanation: The requirement is n ≥ (1.96²)(0.20)(0.80)/(0.06²) ≈ 170.74. Sample size must be rounded up, giving 171.

questions.unit: Unit 5: Regression Analysis
questions.prompt: A regression model predicts a building's daily energy use from outdoor temperature. The residual standard deviation is s = 18 kilowatt-hours. Which interpretation is appropriate?

choices.A: Outdoor temperature typically differs from its predicted value by about 18 degrees.
choices.B: Observed daily energy use typically differs from the line's predicted energy use by about 18 kilowatt-hours.
choices.C: Every building-day has a residual of exactly 18 kilowatt-hours.
choices.D: Outdoor temperature explains exactly 18% of the variation in daily energy use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Observed daily energy use typically differs from the line's predicted energy use by about 18 kilowatt-hours.
questions.explanation: The residual standard deviation describes the typical vertical size of prediction errors in the response variable's units. It is not a slope, a percentage of explained variation, or an exact residual for every case.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: An instructor adds 5 points to every score on an exam. What happens to each student's percentile rank within the class?

choices.A: It increases by 5 percentile points.
choices.B: It is multiplied by 5.
choices.C: It changes only for students originally below the mean.
choices.D: It remains unchanged.

questions.correctAnswerText: It remains unchanged.
questions.explanation: Adding the same constant to all scores preserves their order and all relative ranks, so percentile ranks do not change.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.prompt: Rain is forecast independently on each of the next 14 days with probability 0.20 per day. Which random variable is appropriate for finding the probability that it rains on at least 5 of the days?

choices.A: X = the number of rainy days among the 14 days
choices.B: X = the day on which the fifth rainy day occurs
choices.C: X = the total rainfall amount over the 14 days
choices.D: X = the number of days until the first rainy day

questions.correctAnswerText: X = the number of rainy days among the 14 days
questions.explanation: The event “at least 5 of the days” concerns a count of successes in a fixed number of independent trials, so X should count rainy days among the 14.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: A nonprofit will survey a random sample of eligible voters after an outreach campaign. It wants to estimate the proportion who recall receiving a campaign message. Which parameter should be defined?

choices.A: x, the number of sampled voters who recall a message
choices.B: p̂, the sample proportion of surveyed voters who recall a message
choices.C: p, the proportion of all eligible voters who recall receiving a campaign message
choices.D: μ, the mean number of messages received by sampled voters

questions.correctAnswerText: p, the proportion of all eligible voters who recall receiving a campaign message
questions.explanation: The parameter is a numerical characteristic of the entire target population. The sample count and sample proportion are statistics used to estimate it.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: A laboratory computes a 95% one-sided upper confidence bound of 4.8 milligrams per liter for the population mean nitrate concentration. The safety benchmark is μ < 5 milligrams per liter. Which interpretation is best?

choices.A: At least 95% of individual nitrate measurements are below 4.8 milligrams per liter.
choices.B: There is a 95% probability that μ is below 4.8 milligrams per liter.
choices.C: The sample mean must equal 4.8 milligrams per liter because the bound is below 5.
choices.D: The procedure provides evidence at the corresponding one-sided 5% level that μ is below 5, but it does not describe every individual measurement.

questions.correctAnswerText: The procedure provides evidence at the corresponding one-sided 5% level that μ is below 5, but it does not describe every individual measurement.
questions.explanation: The upper bound 4.8 lies below the benchmark 5, so the corresponding one-sided test rejects μ = 5 in favor of μ < 5 at α = 0.05. The bound concerns the population mean, not a stated percentage of individual values.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: A dataset of n > 1 observations has mean x̄ and positive sample standard deviation s. One additional observation equal to x̄ is added. How do the sample mean and sample standard deviation change?

choices.A: The mean increases and the standard deviation decreases.
choices.B: The mean stays the same and the standard deviation decreases.
choices.C: The mean stays the same and the standard deviation stays exactly the same.
choices.D: The mean decreases and the standard deviation increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: The mean stays the same and the standard deviation decreases.
questions.explanation: Adding a value equal to the old mean leaves the mean and the sum of squared deviations unchanged. The sample-variance denominator increases from n − 1 to n, so the positive standard deviation decreases.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: Two independent random samples are used for a two-sample t procedure comparing population means. The sample standard deviations differ substantially. Which statement is correct about the usual unpooled two-sample t procedure?

choices.A: It is invalid unless the two sample standard deviations are exactly equal.
choices.B: It requires combining the two sample standard deviations into one pooled estimate.
choices.C: It does not require the two population variances to be equal, though unusual shapes and small samples can still be concerns.
choices.D: It becomes a paired t procedure whenever the sample sizes are equal.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not require the two population variances to be equal, though unusual shapes and small samples can still be concerns.
questions.explanation: The unpooled procedure estimates each sample's contribution to the standard error separately. Equal variances and equal sample sizes are not requirements.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.prompt: Let X be the number of 12 independently generated passwords that contain a special symbol, where each password has probability 0.30 of containing one. Calculator output gives P(X ≤ 2) = 0.253 and P(X ≤ 5) = 0.961. What is P(3 ≤ X ≤ 5)?
questions.explanation: The event 3 ≤ X ≤ 5 is obtained by subtracting cumulative probabilities: P(X ≤ 5) − P(X ≤ 2) = 0.961 − 0.253 = 0.708.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: In a random sample of 100 items, 32 meet a standard. For testing H0: p = 0.40 against Ha: p < 0.40, which is the approximate test statistic and p-value?

choices.A: z = −0.80 and p-value = 0.212
choices.B: z = −1.33 and p-value = 0.092
choices.C: z = −1.63 and p-value = 0.103
choices.D: z = −1.63 and p-value = 0.051

questions.correctAnswerText: z = −1.63 and p-value = 0.051
questions.explanation: z = (0.32 − 0.40)/√[0.40(0.60)/100] ≈ −1.63. For the left-tailed alternative, the standard normal area below −1.63 is about 0.051.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: A study of adolescent sleep asks parents to report the usual bedtime of their teenagers. What potential problem is most directly introduced by this choice?

choices.A: Placebo effect, because parents know they are reporting sleep behavior
choices.B: Measurement bias from proxy reports that may not accurately reflect the teenagers' actual bedtimes
choices.C: Confounding caused by randomly assigning parents to report bedtimes
choices.D: Undercoverage of parents who know their teenagers' bedtimes

questions.correctAnswerText: Measurement bias from proxy reports that may not accurately reflect the teenagers' actual bedtimes
questions.explanation: Parents may not observe the true bedtime or may report it inaccurately. This is a measurement problem caused by using proxies, not random assignment or undercoverage as described.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: A park manager wants to compare mean trail-use counts on summer weekdays with mean trail-use counts on winter weekdays. Which design best supports inference about the difference?

choices.A: Randomly select weekdays from each season and record the trail-use count on every selected day.
choices.B: Use the busiest summer weekday and the quietest winter weekday.
choices.C: Record summer counts at the main entrance and winter counts at a side entrance.
choices.D: Let visitors choose which season's count they want to contribute to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Randomly select weekdays from each season and record the trail-use count on every selected day.
questions.explanation: Random selection within each season gives representative independent samples for estimating and comparing the two seasonal population means.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: Two independent studies test the same null value for a population proportion. Both have the same observed difference p̂ − p0 = 0.04, but the first uses n = 200 and the second uses n = 2,000. The second study has a much smaller p-value. Which interpretation is best?

choices.A: The effect observed in the second study is ten times as large.
choices.B: The second study proves that the null value is impossible.
choices.C: The estimated effect is the same, but the larger sample gives a smaller standard error and stronger statistical evidence.
choices.D: The smaller p-value shows that the second study used a less representative sample.

questions.correctAnswerText: The estimated effect is the same, but the larger sample gives a smaller standard error and stronger statistical evidence.
questions.explanation: The two point estimates are equally far from the null value. Increasing n decreases the standard error, increasing the magnitude of the test statistic and decreasing the p-value without changing the estimated effect size.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: For each patient, a researcher records the difference between heart rate after and before a breathing exercise. Which display is most appropriate for examining the distribution of the patient-level differences?

choices.A: A segmented bar chart of before and after status
choices.B: A dotplot of the numerical differences
choices.C: A scatterplot with no patient pairing indicated
choices.D: A two-way table of heart-rate categories

questions.correctAnswerText: A dotplot of the numerical differences
questions.explanation: The paired differences form one quantitative variable. A dotplot displays its shape, center, spread, and unusual values directly.

questions.unit: Unit 5: Regression Analysis
questions.stimulus: For 20 city blocks, x is tree-canopy coverage (percent) and y is afternoon sidewalk temperature (degrees Celsius). The least-squares line is ŷ = 38 − 0.20x. The sample means are x̄ = 35 and ȳ = 31. A twenty-first block is added with x = 35 and y = 31.
questions.prompt: For the original 20 blocks, ŷ = 38 − 0.20x, x̄ = 35, and ȳ = 31. What happens to the least-squares regression line after the block (35, 31) is added?

choices.A: Its slope becomes more negative because the new point is below all points with x = 35.
choices.B: Its slope becomes 0 because the new point is at the sample means.
choices.C: Its intercept increases to 38.2 because the sample size increases.
choices.D: The fitted line remains ŷ = 38 − 0.20x.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fitted line remains ŷ = 38 − 0.20x.
questions.explanation: The added point is exactly (x̄, ȳ), which lies on the existing line because 38 − 0.20(35) = 31. It contributes zero to both centered cross-products and centered squared x deviations, so the fitted line is unchanged.

questions.unit: Unit 5: Regression Analysis
questions.stimulus: For 20 city blocks, x is tree-canopy coverage (percent) and y is afternoon sidewalk temperature (degrees Celsius). The least-squares line is ŷ = 38 − 0.20x. The sample means are x̄ = 35 and ȳ = 31. A twenty-first block is added with x = 35 and y = 31.
questions.prompt: For the original 20 blocks, ŷ = 38 − 0.20x, x̄ = 35, and ȳ = 31. What happens to the sum of squared residuals after the block (35, 31) is added?

choices.A: It must increase because there is one more observation.
choices.B: It decreases by 31².
choices.C: It remains unchanged.
choices.D: It becomes 0.

questions.correctAnswerText: It remains unchanged.
questions.explanation: The existing fitted values and residuals do not change, and the added point lies exactly on the line, so its residual and squared residual are both zero.

questions.unit: Unit 5: Regression Analysis
questions.stimulus: For 20 city blocks, x is tree-canopy coverage (percent) and y is afternoon sidewalk temperature (degrees Celsius). The least-squares line is ŷ = 38 − 0.20x. The sample means are x̄ = 35 and ȳ = 31. A twenty-first block is added with x = 35 and y = 31.
questions.prompt: For the original 20 blocks, ŷ = 38 − 0.20x, x̄ = 35, and ȳ = 31. How should the added point (35, 31) be characterized relative to the fitted relationship?

choices.A: It has residual 0 and is not a high-leverage point because its x-value is at the center of the x-values.
choices.B: It has residual 7 and is a high-leverage point because its y-value is large.
choices.C: It has residual −7 and must substantially change the slope.
choices.D: It has residual 0 but is a high-leverage point because every point on the line has high leverage.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has residual 0 and is not a high-leverage point because its x-value is at the center of the x-values.
questions.explanation: Its predicted value is 38 − 0.20(35) = 31, equal to its observed value. Leverage depends on unusual x-position, and x = x̄ is central rather than extreme.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.prompt: A meteorologist wants to examine whether a high-ozone day makes a high-ozone day more likely on the following day. Which plan best supplies data for comparing the relevant conditional probabilities while limiting overlap among observations?

choices.A: Select only high-ozone days and count how many are followed by high-ozone days.
choices.B: Randomly select many well-separated dates, record ozone status on each selected date and the next date, and compare next-day high-ozone rates for the two initial-day statuses.
choices.C: Record the total number of high-ozone days in one year without preserving their order.
choices.D: Ask residents whether they remember two high-ozone days occurring in succession.

questions.correctAnswerText: Randomly select many well-separated dates, record ozone status on each selected date and the next date, and compare next-day high-ozone rates for the two initial-day statuses.
questions.explanation: Recording both statuses for randomly selected, well-separated day pairs permits comparison of P(next high | initial high) with P(next high | initial not high) while reducing overlap among pairs.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: A one-proportion z-test of H0: p = 0.25 with n = 400 produces z = 2.31. What sample proportion was observed, approximately?

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: For a random sample of 9 package masses, the sum of the squared deviations from the sample mean is 162 square kilograms. What is the sample variance?

choices.A: 20.25 square kilograms
choices.B: 9.0 square kilograms
choices.C: 4.5 square kilograms
choices.D: 2.25 square kilograms

questions.correctAnswerText: 20.25 square kilograms
questions.explanation: Sample variance divides the sum of squared deviations by n − 1. Thus s² = 162/(9 − 1) = 162/8 = 20.25 square kilograms.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: A matched-pairs study enrolls 30 participants and records a measurement before and after a program. Four participants have no after-program measurement and are excluded. What degrees of freedom should be used for the paired t procedure based on the complete pairs?
questions.explanation: Only the 26 participants with both measurements contribute paired differences. A paired t procedure on 26 differences has df = 26 − 1 = 25.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.prompt: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled, and X is the absolute difference between the two results. What does P(X = 0) = 1/6 represent?

choices.A: At least one die shows 0 on one sixth of rolls.
choices.B: The two dice show the same number on 6 of the 36 equally likely ordered outcomes.
choices.C: The sum of the two dice is 0 on one sixth of rolls.
choices.D: The second die is determined by the first die on every roll.

questions.correctAnswerText: The two dice show the same number on 6 of the 36 equally likely ordered outcomes.
questions.explanation: An absolute difference of 0 occurs exactly for (1,1), (2,2), ..., (6,6). Those 6 matching outcomes among 36 equally likely ordered pairs give probability 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: A small company attempts a census of all employees about workplace injuries, but some employees do not respond and others misreport minor injuries. Which statement is correct?

choices.A: A census eliminates sampling variability but does not eliminate nonresponse or measurement error.
choices.B: A census automatically eliminates all forms of bias.
choices.C: Nonresponse can matter only when a random sample, rather than a census, is used.
choices.D: Misreporting is sampling error and disappears when every employee is contacted.

questions.correctAnswerText: A census eliminates sampling variability but does not eliminate nonresponse or measurement error.
questions.explanation: Attempting to contact the full population removes random sampling variability, but missing responses and inaccurate measurements can still bias the result.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: A test uses H0: p = 0.50 and Ha: p > 0.50. The observed sample proportion is 0.45, giving a negative z statistic. Which conclusion is appropriate?

choices.A: Reject H0 because the sample proportion differs from 0.50.
choices.B: Reject H0 because every negative z statistic is significant.
choices.C: Conclude that p < 0.50 because that is the stated alternative.
choices.D: Fail to reject H0; the result is in the direction opposite to Ha and the right-tailed p-value is large.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fail to reject H0; the result is in the direction opposite to Ha and the right-tailed p-value is large.
questions.explanation: For Ha: p > 0.50, evidence lies in the positive-z tail. A negative statistic places most of the normal curve to its right, so the p-value is large.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: For a fixed numerical dataset, consider S(c) = Σ(xᵢ − c)². At which value of c is S(c) minimized?

choices.A: The minimum observation
choices.B: The median
choices.C: The mean
choices.D: The maximum observation

questions.correctAnswerText: The mean
questions.explanation: The arithmetic mean is the least-squares center: the sum of squared deviations from c is minimized when c = x̄.
